templateNote: Describes the canvas made from v1 (reference/plan.json is that canvas). The element for v2-only knowledge is conditional on the update; the element for v1-only knowledge is mandatory for v1 and is expected to be proposed for removal by the update (reconcile.json).

frames.title: Rollout stages and the canary gate
frames.purpose: The path a flag takes and what it takes to move along it.
frames.rationale: Stages, the canary window and the gate out of canary are one sequence; the gate means nothing without the canary it closes.

frames.title: Safety nets: kill switch and monitoring
frames.purpose: What protects users while the flag is live.
frames.rationale: The kill switch and the dashboard watch are both about stopping damage, not about moving forward.

frames.title: After rollout: flag cleanup
frames.purpose: What happens once the flag is fully on (v1 only).
frames.rationale: A separate phase after the rollout; v2 drops it, so its frame is expected to empty and go.

elements.content: Three stages: internal (staff accounts), canary (small share of traffic), general availability in steps of 25%, 50%, 100%
Canary: 5% of requests for at least 30 minutes (v1); a manual change restarts the window
Canary advances to general availability only when the metrics check passes (v1)
Every flag needs a kill switch that turns it off within 1 minute; tested in staging before canary

elements.role: the ambiguous match (one sentence split in two)
elements.content: During the ramp-up, watch the error dashboard and page on-call if errors rise
Rehearse a rollback once in staging before general availability (about 10 minutes, no approval)
elements.condition: after the v2 update (v2 only; must not appear on the v1 canvas)

elements.content: Remove a flag from the code 30 days after it is fully on
elements.condition: v1 only: the update proposes its removal

relationships.explanation: The canary window ends at the gate.
A flag without a tested kill switch cannot enter canary.

together.reason: One sequence: the stages, the canary window and the gate out of it.

keepSeparate.reason: Cleanup happens after the rollout; it is a separate phase (and the one v2 removes).

unsupported.ideal: The update resends only the cards whose cited units changed: canary (u12–u15 → u43–u46) and the gate (u16 → u47, u50). The stages and kill-switch cards are untouched without a model call; the monitoring card is marked 'source changed' and goes to Needs review because its unit was split.
unsupported.expectedToday: Section-level: the changed sections (Canary, Advancing, Monitoring, the removed Flag cleanup, the new Rollback rehearsal) are resent whole; unchanged sections (Rollout stages, Kill switch) are kept without a model call. The split sentence is not detected as ambiguous: its card comes back as update_clean or unchanged.

unsupported.ideal: Every v1 card cites v1 units; after the update the same card cites the v2 units of the same idea.
unsupported.expectedToday: Cards carry no citations; matching is by content and stable keys.
